subject.title: CLI-backed helper paths still bypass CLI dispatch on latest main

question: Where should OpenClaw perform CLI runtime resolution for remaining helper paths so probes, slug generation, startup/prewarm, and subagent/gateway registration match dispatch without storing CLI runtime ids as canonical model providers?
rationale: The code evidence shows real divergence, but the permanent boundary affects auth diagnostics, billing safety, session metadata, and canonical provider semantics, so automation should not choose that architecture alone.

options.title: Resolve At Dispatch Boundaries
options.body: Add a shared execution-provider handoff near helper dispatch and run registration while keeping persisted model/provider state canonical; this best matches current accepted followup and attempt-execution patterns.

options.title: Keep Some Helpers Embedded
options.body: Explicitly decide that auth probes or slug generation remain embedded diagnostics, then document and test the intentional mismatch so it does not look like a CLI dispatch bug.

options.title: Split Narrow Items First
options.body: Keep this broad tracker open but land or close the narrower open probe, memory-gate, and subagent items before attempting a single cross-surface repair.

recommendation.title: Resolve At Dispatch Boundaries
recommendation.body: Add a shared execution-provider handoff near helper dispatch and run registration while keeping persisted model/provider state canonical; this best matches current accepted followup and attempt-execution patterns.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the accepted followup repair and is the best available routing owner for deciding whether the remaining cross-surface boundary should be dispatch-time or helper-specific.
